seo.title: EU AI Act and ISO/IEC 42001 Evidence Pack | VipraTech
seo.description: Testing evidence, risk records and technical documentation for AI features, mapped to EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF for counsel and auditors.

problem.intro: Enterprise customers and auditors are starting to ask SaaS and AI vendors for evidence about their AI systems: what they do, how they were tested, how risks are managed and how people oversee them. The information exists in tickets, notebooks, test logs and engineers' heads, but not in a form counsel or an auditor can review.

pain_points.title: Evidence scattered across teams
pain_points.detail: Model choices, evaluations, red-team results and incidents sit in different tools owned by different people.

pain_points.title: Unclear mapping to requirements
pain_points.detail: Teams are unsure which EU AI Act obligations or ISO/IEC 42001 controls their evidence supports.

pain_points.title: Testing that was never recorded
pain_points.detail: Security and safety testing happened, but results, versions and fixes were not kept in an auditable form.

pain_points.title: Customer due diligence pressure
pain_points.detail: Large customers send AI-specific questionnaires and expect consistent, documented answers.

solution.overview: We build an evidence pack for one or more AI features. We start with an inventory: what each system does, which models and data it uses, who uses it and where it runs. We then gather the technical evidence and, where gaps exist, produce it: architecture and data flow records, evaluation and red-team results, security test reports, logging and monitoring design, human oversight points and an incident process. Each item is mapped to relevant EU AI Act obligations, ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A controls and NIST AI RMF functions in a traceability matrix. Risk classification notes are prepared for your counsel to decide. The pack is designed to be maintained as features change, not rebuilt for each audit.
capabilities: AI system inventory with purpose, models, data, users and deployment
Technical documentation of architecture, data flows and model choices
Security and safety testing records with versions and fixes
Human oversight and logging design records
Traceability matrix to EU AI Act obligations, ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A controls and NIST AI RMF
Gap list with owners, and a process to keep the pack current

workflow.title: Inventory AI systems
workflow.detail: We list each AI feature with its purpose, users, models, data sources and deployment.

workflow.title: Gather existing evidence
workflow.detail: We collect architecture notes, evaluations, test reports, incidents and policies from your teams.

workflow.title: Fill testing gaps
workflow.detail: Where testing is missing, we run focused security and safety tests and record the results.

workflow.title: Map to requirements
workflow.detail: Evidence is mapped to EU AI Act obligations, ISO/IEC 42001 controls and NIST AI RMF functions.

workflow.title: Counsel and GRC review
workflow.detail: Your counsel reviews the risk classification notes, and your GRC lead approves the pack and gap list.

workflow.title: Maintain
workflow.detail: Owners and triggers are set so the pack is updated when features, models or data change.

inputs: List of AI features and their owners
Existing evaluation, pentest and red-team reports

Customer and auditor questionnaires already received
outputs: Testing records with versions and fixes

human_in_the_loop: Your counsel decides risk classification under the EU AI Act, and your GRC lead approves the pack and accepts or assigns each gap. Certification decisions rest with your accredited auditor.

Issue trackers such as Jira or Linear

guardrails: No compliance or certification claims made in the pack
Every statement linked to a source document or test record
Classification notes clearly marked for counsel decision
Access to the pack limited to named roles
Version history kept for every update
compliance_notes: Designed to support, not replace, legal assessment under the EU AI Act and certification audits against ISO/IEC 42001.
NIST AI RMF mapping helps US-facing customers compare your evidence with their own risk programmes.

pilot.scope: One customer-facing AI feature, from inventory to traceability matrix, including a focused security test where evidence is missing.

what_we_measure.how: Share of mapped requirements with at least one linked source document or test record.

Time taken to update the pack after a simulated model change.

faqs.q: Will this make us compliant with the EU AI Act?
faqs.a: No single document does that. The pack organises the technical evidence the Act and your counsel will ask for, and shows where gaps remain. Legal classification and conformity decisions stay with your counsel and, where relevant, notified bodies.

That is a business decision, often driven by customer demand. The pack is useful either way, because the same evidence answers customer questionnaires and supports an AI management system if you pursue certification.

faqs.q: Does this replace our GRC tool?
faqs.a: No, it feeds it. Evidence and mappings can be exported into Vanta, Drata or your existing register.

faqs.q: Is our system high-risk under the EU AI Act?
faqs.a: That depends on its intended purpose and use, and it is a legal question for your counsel. We prepare clear notes on what the system does and who uses it to inform that decision.
